absent: Handle encoding and translation among handles, objects, locations and class indices.
Memory layout of zspage, size_class and zs_pool beyond members observed in use.
Allocation, free, read and write paths for individual compressed objects.
Isolation and putback helpers for source and destination groups and fullness thresholds.
Movable isolate implementation and descriptor helpers for mapping and accounting.
Zone state accounting semantics and reference counting for descriptors.
Shrinker batch meaning and stop sentinel value.
Full statistics structure and debug interfaces.
Compression, store, load, reclaim and writeback flows for swap entries.

findings.text: Export zs_create_pool accepts a name and returns a pool reference on success and a null indicator on failure after unwinding partial state through the destroy path.
Export zs_destroy_pool tears down a pool after releasing shrinker, pending migration work and statistics and then freeing owned classes, name and pool storage.
Export zs_compact compacts classes from large to small and returns total pages reclaimed, with concurrent callers receiving no progress due to single flight control.
Export zs_pool_stats copies the current pool statistics into a caller provided statistics object.
Export zswap_stored_pages is a globally visible atomic long counter for stored compressed pages.

Pool object for compressed swap combines a backing allocator pool with per processor compression state, a reference count allowing reinitialization, membership linkage for the global collection, deferred release work, a hotplug linkage node and a fixed size algorithm name store.
Compression context bundles an asynchronous compression handle with its request, a wait state for completion, a linear buffer and a mutual exclusion guard serializing use.

Swap entry record associates a swap identifier with a compressed length, a referenced flag, an owning pool reference, a handle value, an object cgroup linkage and list linkage for recency, while per swap file tree pointers and counts are kept in separate indexed arrays.

Migration acquires the pool guard in write mode first, then the class spin guard, then attempts the page write guard without blocking, and releases in reverse order with matching unwind on contention failure.

Compaction holds the pool write guard outermost with the class spin guard inside, temporarily drops both to allow scheduling when the destination becomes full or the pool guard shows contention, then reacquires in the same order before continuing.

Deferred freeing splices the empty fullness queue under the class guard into a private collection, then for each queued page holds its page guard while rechecking class association and updating accounting under the class guard during release.
The global pool collection is guarded by a dedicated spin guard, taken with bottom half suppression during empty notification and required held for current pool retrieval and compressor lookup.

Size classes with identical geometry may share one object, recognized because the stored index differs from the slot position, and such shared slots are skipped during freeing, compaction, counting and destruction.
The number of physical pages backing a compressed page group is one when the class size is a power of two, otherwise the smallest waste choice across the allowed chain range is selected.

Only one compaction pass runs at a time per pool through an atomic exchange flag, with concurrent callers returning no progress, and total reclaimed pages are accumulated into a compacted statistic before clearing the flag.

Migration succeeds immediately for descriptors lacking an associated group, otherwise it secures guards, marks the replacement descriptor, transfers content, reassigns live handles to the new location preserving object position and class association, swaps the subpage linkage, then fixes zone accounting and retires the old descriptor.

Compaction repeatedly ensures a destination group exists, obtains a source group, attempts its write guard, moves contents to the destination, returns the source to its fullness tracking and frees it when empty, recycling the destination when full or under contention.

Creation initializes deferred work, locking and flags, duplicates the name, builds size classes from large to small with sharing when possible, initializes fullness queues, then attaches optional statistics and shrinker support before returning, destroying everything on any failure.

Compressed pool setup allocates the pool object and backing allocator, prepares per processor state and hotplug membership and reference tracking, and on failure releases hotplug membership, per processor contexts, backing allocator and the pool object.

When the last reference drops, the pool is removed from the global collection under guard and deferred work is scheduled that synchronizes read copy update grace, exits reference tracking and destroys hotplug state, compression contexts, backing allocator and the pool object.
A movable operations table exposes isolate, migrate and putback hooks for the allocator type, with the putback hook defined as having no action in these fragments.

Shrinker scan triggers compaction and reports reclaimed pages or a stop sentinel when none, count estimates reclaimable pages across owned classes, registration creates a named shrinker with zero batch and pool association, and unregistration releases it.
Initialization creates handle and page group caches and then registers movable handling and statistics, while teardown unregisters movable handling, releases statistics and destroys the caches.

Contention on the page write guard during migration is reported as busy rather than retryable, reflecting unbounded holder duration from slow processing or preemption combined with bounded immediate retries that cannot assure timely success.
A noted risk is that a group isolated for migration may be destroyed while its page guard is temporarily dropped, suggesting future deferral of destruction until return from isolation.
Destruction checks every fullness queue of each owned class and emits a diagnostic when any queue remains occupied, yet proceeds to release class, name and pool storage.
Address space shift is fourteen and the corresponding page count is one shifted left by that amount.
Default maximum pool size is twenty percent and the acceptance threshold is ninety percent of that maximum.
The unset sentinel for textual parameters is an empty string.
Lookup by compressor name under guard walks the global collection with read copy update protection and returns only an entry whose reference acquisition succeeds, skipping entries being destroyed.

Fallback creation verifies compressor availability, and when the configured choice is missing but differs from the build default it reports the issue and reverts to the default, abandoning creation with a one time warning if the default is also unavailable.
Deferred freeing has an active variant that flushes pending work and initializes the work item to the asynchronous handler, alongside an inline inactive variant that performs no action.

Per processor compression states are allocated zeroed, torn down individually per possible processor with request, handle and buffer release handling null and error cases, then the per processor area itself is freed.

Shrink coordination combines a spin guard with a next target cgroup pointer, a work item and a shrinker pointer, separate from a global recency list, a dedicated workqueue and a flag recording whether the pool has reached full.
Operational health is tracked through stored page counts distinguishing incompressible content and through hit, writeback, reject and decompress failure tallies.
Enable control uses custom set with standard boolean retrieval, while compressor selection uses custom set with standard string retrieval and release, defaulting to the build configured compressor.
Initialization tracks a count of created pools plus a tri state of uninitialized, success or failure, guarded by a dedicated mutex with a separate flag indicating whether any pool exists.
Current pool retrieval asserts the collection guard is held and delegates to an internal helper that performs the actual selection.

During reverse class construction a one time huge threshold is established from the first multi page single object geometry, adjusted downward to account for handle overhead added before class lookup.
Diagnostic output for this compressed swap component uses a module name prefix applied through a format wrapper, with pool specific debug linking a message to the pool algorithm name.
When migration moves content across zones, zone page accounting is decremented for the old descriptor zone and incremented for the new descriptor zone after acquiring a reference on the replacement.
